ko.executive_summary: Qualcomm is actively evaluating and confirming Samsung's 2nm process for next-generation Snapdragon flagship chips, with Samsung achieving near 60% 2nm yield. Simultaneously, Qualcomm is expanding Snapdragon's footprint into personal AI devices beyond smartphones, supported by renewed Apple patent collaboration. AI is becoming integral to chipmaking design workflows via EDA tools and systems like OpenAI's Jalapeño.
key_facts: Qualcomm evaluating Samsung's 2nm process for future Snapdragon chips
Qualcomm confirmed Apple patent renewal and Snapdragon adoption
Snapdragon expansion into personal AI device category
TSMC affiliate planning second Singapore packaging plant due to AI demand
Samsung and Verizon completed ISAC trial in Dallas for 6G virtualized network sensing

implications.text: Qualcomm's Samsung 2nm evaluation signals potential production diversification away from TSMC, though current demand fills TSMC affiliate's first Singapore plant indicating no imminent capacity crisis for incumbents.
Snapdragon expansion into personal AI devices creates new revenue stream beyond smartphones, positioning Qualcomm in emerging edge AI market competing against custom silicon designs.
AI-assisted chipmaking tools reducing design cycles accelerates time-to-market, potentially lowering barriers for new chip architects and pressuring traditional EDA vendors.

ko.counterpoint: Samsung's 2nm yield at 60% remains below production thresholds for immediate high-volume deployment, and Qualcomm's evaluation does not guarantee adoption.
